description.en: The most important purification and confession practice in Tibetan Buddhism. Seventeen phrases, about one hundred syllables.
description.zh: 藏传佛教中最重要的净化业障与忏悔修法。共十七句，约一百个音节。

practiceNotes.en: Vajrasattva practice purifies negative karma and broken commitments. It is done with the Four Opponent Powers: (1) the power of support — taking refuge and generating bodhicitta; (2) the power of regret — sincere regret for harmful actions; (3) the power of resolve — determining not to repeat them; (4) the power of the remedy — reciting the mantra while visualizing Vajrasattva above your head, white and radiant, with purifying nectar flowing down through your body and washing away all negativity and obscurations. At the end, Vajrasattva dissolves into you, and you rest in the recognition that your mind is pure. Traditionally, 21 recitations a day are said to stop negativity from increasing, and 100,000 recitations are part of the foundational practices (ngöndro).
practiceNotes.zh: 金刚萨埵修法净化恶业与毁损的誓言，需具足"四力"：（一）依止力——皈依并发菩提心；（二）破恶力——对过去恶业生起真诚的追悔；（三）防护力——决心不再重犯；（四）对治力——持诵此咒，观想金刚萨埵在头顶，身白色光明，甘露从其身流下，注入并充满自身，洗净一切罪障。最后金刚萨埵融入自身，安住于自心本净之中。传统上说，每日念二十一遍可令罪业不再增长；十万遍为加行（前行）修法的一部分。

verifyNotes: Phrase 8: spelling of siddhiṃ me (མེ vs མྨེ) differs between editions; this follows the reference screenshot.
Phrase 10: śreyaḥ is spelled ཤྲི་ཡཿ here; some editions use ཤྲེ་ཡཿ or ཤྲཱི་ཡཾ. Tibetan phonetics "shriyam" follow common practice texts.
